brief: I work on growth finance at Grüns (https://gruns.co). Compare two acquisition channels over the first three 28-day shipment periods using these entirely hypothetical exercise inputs, not Grüns results or prices. Each channel acquires 100 subscribers in period 1. Paid social costs $4,800 to acquire that cohort and produces 100, 70, and 54 delivered orders in periods 1–3; affiliates cost $5,800 in total acquisition fees and produce 100, 82, and 70 delivered orders. Every delivered order has $50 net revenue and $22 total variable product, fulfillment, and shipping cost. Acquisition costs occur only in period 1; there are no other costs, refunds, or new customers in this exercise. Write a Markdown decision memo under 550 words with per-period and cumulative contribution after acquisition cost, the payback period for each cohort, and a recommendation about which channel looks stronger within this observation window. Explain why a higher repeat-order rate alone does not settle the spending decision, and name two missing inputs needed before scaling. Do not extrapolate a lifetime value beyond the supplied periods or present the exercise figures as public company facts.

I'm the accessibility content lead for a proposed Grüns (https://gruns.co) product-page redesign. Create a Markdown image-text handoff for the following eight hypothetical design assets; these descriptions are exercise inputs, not an inventory of our live site. A: a product photo showing an outer pouch labeled 'Grüns Superfood Gummies' beside a sealed daily packet; B: a close-up of the gummies showing their bear shape; C: a hand tearing open a packet beside the visible caption 'Rip'; D: gummies tipped into a palm beside the visible caption 'Tip'; E: an exact repeat of image A beside a second purchase button; F: an abstract green wave behind a heading already present as real text; G: a bear icon inside the same account link as the visible words 'My account'; H: a badge image whose only text is '3rd party tested', with no equivalent nearby text. For each asset, give its purpose, proposed alt text or empty-alt decision, and any required treatment of the surrounding link or caption. Keep proposed nonempty alt text under 110 characters and the whole handoff under 500 words. Finish with two checks the implementer should make in the rendered page. Use the supplied descriptions without inventing colors, quantities, label details, or health benefits; verify brand/product terminology against the official site.

I'm a customer success manager at Linear (https://linear.app). A customer wants to clean up issue labels without losing useful reporting. Treat this as a hypothetical workspace: its Web, Mobile, Platform, and Customer Experience teams currently use these 12 labels inconsistently: bug, Bug, feature, feat, ios, android, web, urgent, P1, in-progress, blocked, and customer-escalation. Propose a practical Markdown taxonomy plan under 650 words. Include a 12-row mapping from each existing label to its proposed destination, a short definition of each retained label, and a five-step rollout that protects saved views and existing issues. Explain where native priority, workflow status, or issue relations are more appropriate than a label, without assuming every blocked issue already has a known blocking issue. The model must support an issue affecting both iOS and Android. Verify current label scope and grouping behavior in official Linear documentation, cite the relevant pages, and clearly distinguish product behavior from your recommended governance. Deliver a reviewable plan only; do not access or change a workspace.

I'm helping a Linear (https://linear.app) Enterprise customer plan access before inviting collaborators. These are three hypothetical exercise situations: payroll-correction issues should be visible only to five finance employees; an external designer should work with the Design team without gaining routine access to unrelated teams; and an engineer outside a private Security team needs to collaborate on one vulnerability issue without seeing the team's other work. Write a Markdown access-design memo under 650 words. For each situation, give the recommended role/team/sharing configuration, who can see and edit the relevant work, and a concrete check an admin should perform before approving access. Add a short explanation of why a project's visibility needs separate attention when public and private teams both contribute, plus three checks covering integrations, exports, or APIs. Use current official Linear documentation and link the pages supporting consequential permissions claims. State any verified Enterprise requirements and limitations; do not invent a view-only role or assume that a private team prevents all downstream disclosure. No live account access or changes are needed.

I work on customer education at Allbirds (https://www.allbirds.com). Build a reader-facing shoe-care companion as one standalone responsive HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript, no external libraries, fonts, or image assets. Use the current official care guide at https://www.allbirds.com/pages/shoe-care and relevant product-specific guidance. A reader should choose a full clean, a quick surface clean, or laces/insoles care and get a short actionable checklist. Before offering machine-washing instructions, ask whether the reader has confirmed that their particular model's care guidance permits it; include a useful 'I'm not sure' path. Let readers check off steps, see their progress, and reset the checklist; changing the selected path must not retain misleading completion marks. Give it a warm, tactile field-guide feel with strong typography and numbered steps. Keep warnings and model exceptions beside the relevant action, make controls keyboard accessible with visible focus, and retain useful guidance if JavaScript is unavailable. Include dated official source links. This is a local prototype: no account connection, shopping checkout, data submission, or promise that all Allbirds models can be cleaned the same way.

I work on sustainability sourcing at Allbirds (https://www.allbirds.com). Recommend an emissions-reduction package using the following entirely hypothetical exercise inputs, not Allbirds product measurements, supplier quotes, or commitments. We will make 10,000 pairs with an assumed baseline of 8.0 kg CO2e per pair within a fixed cradle-to-customer boundary. Option A changes a material and saves 0.60 kg CO2e per pair at an added $0.70 per pair; B changes factory energy and saves 0.50 kg at $0.45 per pair; C changes transportation and saves 0.20 kg at $0.30 per pair. Assume savings are independent and additive, all three options cover the full production run, and there are no setup costs. The added-spend cap is $10,000. Write a Markdown recommendation under 550 words with a table comparing all seven nonempty option combinations on added cost, total emissions saved, and budget feasibility. Choose the feasible package with the greatest total reduction, show its new per-pair footprint and cost per metric tonne avoided, and name two validations required before making a real sourcing decision. Use Allbirds' current official sustainability information for context, link it, and keep the supplied partial-boundary exercise separate from any public whole-life or carbon-neutrality claim.

I run customer education at Ramp (https://ramp.com). Write a 20-minute accounts-payable fraud tabletop for a customer's finance team, in Markdown and under 650 words. This scenario is entirely hypothetical: a long-standing vendor has a legitimate $48,000 invoice due tomorrow, but a new email asks the team to replace its bank details immediately; the sender's display name matches the usual contact, the domain contains a look-alike character, and the only callback number is in that email. A Ramp bill also displays a potential-fraud alert. Give the facilitator a timed agenda, an opening scenario, two later injects that test whether the team independently verifies the change, and a six-item observer checklist. Include expected safe responder actions and three debrief questions, without declaring the invoice or new account fraudulent before verification. Ground Ramp-specific behavior and escalation guidance in the current official Bill Pay Fraud and vendor-verification help pages, with links. Do not imply an alert guarantees detection or that an invoice's existing approval verifies changed payment instructions. Use role names and fictional details only; the exercise must not require sending a message, calling a vendor, changing bank details, or releasing a payment.

I'm preparing a Ramp (https://ramp.com) card-reconciliation training example for a customer's finance analyst. All entries below are hypothetical exercise data in USD, with no other transactions, payments, fees, or foreign exchange: H1 hotel authorization, +300, pending; H2 final hotel charge for the same stay, +240, posted; A1 airline purchase, +600, posted; A2 partial refund linked to A1, -150, posted credit; S1 software purchase, +120, posted. The hotel authorization is still visibly pending at the snapshot time. Write a Markdown reconciliation note under 450 words that calculates posted gross purchases, posted credits, posted net activity, and pending authorizations separately, and explains why summing every visible row is misleading. Include a compact row-by-row classification table and two follow-up checks for the analyst. Verify relevant pending-charge and refund behavior against current official Ramp help documentation and cite it. Do not delete the original purchase from the explanation, assume the hotel hold has already disappeared, describe the net activity as the customer's actual amount due, or invent accounting entries.

I work on guest education at Sweetgreen (https://www.sweetgreen.com). Build a small nutrition-comparison page for three current standard entrées using our official public nutrition guide at https://www.sweetgreen.com/nutrition. If the guide requires a restaurant, choose any current US location and name it; do not ask me for one. Deliver one standalone responsive HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript, no external fonts, images, or libraries. Readers should be able to select up to two of the three items, compare calories, protein, sodium, and published major-allergen information side by side, and clear their selection. Make the selection limit, one-item state, and missing-data state understandable and keyboard accessible. Use a crisp menu-board visual style with a clear numerical comparison table and a restrained green palette. Display the source location and retrieval date, link official sources, and label the values as a static snapshot for standard preparations rather than live availability or customized orders. Keep the shared-kitchen/cross-contact notice visible. Do not infer unlisted allergen status, recommend a medically appropriate meal, rank foods as healthy or unhealthy, or add checkout, an account connection, or any data submission.

I'm a Sweetgreen (https://www.sweetgreen.com) restaurant planning lead. Help me size roasted-sweet-potato prep for a training exercise. These are entirely hypothetical inputs, not our recipes, yields, forecasts, or procedures: 160 lunch orders are expected; 55% use this ingredient; each such order needs 80 g cooked; the planning buffer is 10% above forecast ingredient demand. There are already 2.0 kg cooked and eligible for use under approved procedures. A whole batch uses 4.0 kg raw and yields 78% cooked by weight; partial batches are not possible. Raw supply and cooking capacity are sufficient for any of the scenarios here. Write a Markdown prep recommendation under 500 words. Show cooked demand before and after buffer, additional cooked quantity needed, raw quantity implied before batch rounding, whole batches to prepare, and the resulting cooked overage against unbuffered demand. Include a sensitivity table for 120, 160, and 200 orders with the same mix and yield, plus two observations the manager should check before committing the final batch. Keep all scenario quantities labeled as exercise data and do not create food-safety temperatures, holding limits, or handling procedures.

I'm preparing a Duolingo (https://www.duolingo.com) education-partner briefing for an adult-education program that already uses existing Duolingo for Schools classrooms. Write a Markdown transition pack as of November 12, 2026, under 650 words, using the current official sunset notice at https://duolingoschools.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/44824545841805-Important-information-regarding-Duolingo-for-Schools and related official help pages. Include a short staff briefing that separates what can still be done now, what is already unavailable, and when Schools access ends; a six-item preparation checklist with suggested owner roles; and a learner-facing note of at most 120 words explaining what this means for continued use of the main Duolingo app. Give three dated planning checkpoints before the published sunset. Do not invent a replacement platform, a data-export capability, deletion timing, a migration promise, or changes to learners' subscriptions. Where the program must verify something locally, make it a specific assigned check rather than asking me a follow-up question. Link sources and treat the materials as drafts for program review, not messages to send.

I work in Duolingo (https://www.duolingo.com) partnerships. An employer's learning manager wants evidence before recommending the app as a supplement for adult Spanish and French learners. Write a balanced Markdown evidence digest under 650 words based on the official 2024 report 'Duolingo Path Meets Expectations for Proficiency Outcomes' at https://duolingo-papers.s3.amazonaws.com/reports/Duolingo_whitepaper_language_read_listen_write_speak_2024.pdf and the official efficacy framework at https://blog.duolingo.com/duolingo-efficacy-research-framework/. Include a compact study table covering the population, course stage, skills assessed, assessment instrument, and study design; two or three decision-relevant findings; and three limitations that affect what the employer can infer. Distinguish measured proficiency, engagement, and workplace communication, and identify the report's authorship and publication date. End with three questions the employer should resolve before choosing a learning program. Cite report page numbers for substantive results and link both sources. Do not present this selected study as a current evaluation of every language or feature, convert its findings into a guaranteed time to fluency, or claim a causal advantage over classroom teaching that the design cannot establish.
